Job Description:

Summary:

The Summer College Internship Program is a 10-week paid internship experience that provides undergraduate and graduate students with the opportunity to attend development workshops, network, and be part of our company. Our college interns work on meaningful projects, are mentored under their respective managers, and continue to develop throughout the entire summer. Through the internship program, our interns can attend development workshops that are focused on key business concepts. Interns may work within the skills-based tracks of Business Administration, Information Technology, Actuarial, Human Resources, Analytics & Data, Communications, Finance, Marketing & Sales, Project Management, Clinical Studies, Customer Experience, Digital Operations, and other non-technical and/or technical based degree programs.

- This is a paid 10-week summer internship from the first Monday in June to the second Friday in August (up to 40 hours per week).
- Interns may reside in either a technical or non-technical area.
- Development workshops are provided to help with the transition from school to the corporate environment.
- Housing is not provided as part of our program.

Essential Accountabilities:

- Specific duties will vary by assignment; specific divisional callouts are listed below.
- The Research Insights intern will conduct primary research projects that will help improve the performance of the Health Plan and its affiliates. Primary research will include developing and fielding simple surveys, data analysis, and reporting. In collaboration with team members, the intern will also develop recommendations to improve operational efficiencies and the customer experience.
- Works with a mentor and supports key strategic projects.
- Completes work assignments based on business needs, departmental priorities, and individual qualifications.
- Performs a mix of technical and/or non-technical tasks that will cover a broad range of business-related projects.
- Creates and delivers presentations at completion of internship.
- Consistently demonstrates high standards of integrity by supporting the Lifetime Healthcare Companies' mission and values, adhering to the Corporate Code of Conduct, and leading to the Lifetime Way values and beliefs.
- Maintain confidentiality and protection of member privacy in accordance with the company policies.
- Regular and reliable attendance is expected and required.
- Performs other functions as assigned by management.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Desired Majors/Degree Programs Include: Public Health, Psychology, Business Analytics, Market Research, Business, Mathematics, Marketing, Statistics or similar program(s)
- Preferred (but not required) experience with: Basic experience in survey design, data analysis, and report writing. Highly effective communication and project management skills. Experience with analytical software packages (e.g., SPSS, SAS, R) or survey administration platforms (e.g., Qualtrics, Survey Monkey, Google Forms) is preferred but not required. Must be willing to take additional trainings in the area of survey design and data analysis.
- High School diploma along with proof of continuous college enrollment (enrolled in a full-time undergraduate or graduate degree program).
- Must be in good academic standing.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with ability to interact with technical and non-technical audiences and interface with staff at all levels of the company.
- Ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment while maintaining strong attention to detail changing environment and deliver high-quality work product.
- Ability to work well in a team establishing good working relationships with peers.
- Demonstrates strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving and prioritization skills.
- Proactive approach to work, displaying creativity and flexibility in completing assigned tasks.
- Commitment to continuous improvement of skills and team functioning.
- Self-motivated and able to work independently, as well as on intra- and inter- departmental teams as needed.
- Experience with Microsoft Office Suite.
- Experience using a desktop computer in a professional environment.

Physical Requirements:

- Ability to work while sitting and/or standing at a workstation viewing a computer and using a keyboard, mouse and/or phone for three (3) or more hours at a time.
- Ability to travel across the Health Plan service region for meetings and/or training courses as needed.

The Opportunity:

As a full stack developer, you can resolve a problem with a complete end-to-end solution in a fast, agile environment. If you’re looking for the chance to not just develop software, but to help create a system that will make a difference, we need you on our team. We’re looking for a developer like you with an appetite for learning and the skills needed to develop software and systems from vision to production ready.

This role is more than just coding. As a full stack developer at Booz Allen, you’ll use your passion to learn new tools and techniques and identify needed system improvements. You’ll help clients overcome their most difficult challenges using the latest architectural approaches, tools, and technologies. You’ll help make sure the solution developed by the team considers the current architecture and operating environment, as well as future functionality and enhancements. Due to the nature of work performed within this facility, U.S. citizenship is required.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

- Experience building applications in Java, C++, and or Java Script

- Experience creating solutions to complex problems within a collaborative, cross-functional team

Nice If You Have:

- Experience working with or in the DOW

- Knowledge of Agile methodologies

- Knowledge of Model and Simulation technologies

Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Job Description

Manufacturing Engineering Intern

Summer Internship Program

Our paid Summer Internship Program is designed to provide students with an immersive, hands-on experience within the aerospace and defense industry. Interns work alongside AV team members on meaningful projects involving cutting-edge technology while developing professional relationships, strategic problem-solving skills, and practical experience in a full-time work environment.

This is a 12-week, onsite program intended for highly motivated and passionate students who are currently enrolled in college or are recent graduates. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA, with a preference for students at the junior level or above.

Our program has been recognized by Yello and WayUp as one of the Top 100 Internship Programs in the United States for multiple years.

Depending on the team and location, students who are willing to relocate for their internship may be eligible for a relocation and housing reimbursement stipend.

This position will site onsite in our Pottstown, PA office and will focus on UXS / VideoRay products.

Summary

As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern, you will support the design and operation of manufacturing systems for AV Unmanned Air Vehicles. Under the guidance of experienced manufacturing engineers, you will assist in analyzing production processes and data, help optimize manufacturing workflows, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles. This internship provides hands-on experience in manufacturing process design, factory planning, and production support.

Position Responsibilities

- Assist in supporting and improving manufacturing processes with a focus on efficiency and quality

- Help implement Lean Manufacturing principles and apply Six Sigma methods to support continuous improvement efforts

- Analyze production data such as yields, capacity, cost, and process capability to identify opportunities for improvement

- Support establishment and documentation of standard work hours, sequences, and assembly procedures

- Help generate and update work instructions and other documentation controlling manufacturing processes

- Participate in root cause analysis and problem-solving activities related to materials, design, equipment, and personnel

- Assist in manufacturing capacity planning and factory layout design for improved efficiency

- Support cost estimation activities for new tooling, fixtures, and production equipment

- Collaborate with design engineering teams on Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and reliability analysis

- Participate in cross-functional improvement projects involving engineering and suppliers to enhance cost, cycle time, and quality

- Support Design Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (DFMEA) and Process FMEA (PFMEA) activities

- Provide input to engineering regarding manufacturing considerations for design concepts and specifications

- Gain hands-on experience supporting production floor activities, including assembly and integration processes

- Other duties as assigned

Basic Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Industrial, Mechanical, or a related engineering field

- Some coursework or experience related to manufacturing, process improvement, or quality control

- Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles is a plus

- Basic knowledge of electro-mechanical manufacturing, technical drawings, and Bill of Materials is preferred

- Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook); experience with Visio, Minitab, or CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks) is a plus

- Ability to travel occasionally to supplier sites (up to 10%)

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

- Interest in root cause analysis and continuous improvement techniques

- Effective teamwork and communication skills

- Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

- Demonstrates initiative and responsibility for assigned work

- Commitment to learning and professional growth

Physical Demands

- Ability to work in an office environment (constant)

- Required to sit or stand for extended periods and use computer and office equipment frequently

Clearance Level

No Clearance

Company Description

Jobs for Humanity is collaborating with Upwardly Global and with Jet Propulsion Laboratory to build an inclusive and just employment ecosystem. We support individuals coming from all walks of life.

Company Name: Jet Propulsion Laboratory

Job Description

Postdoc: MDL- Microdevice And Sensor Systems

Location: JPL Campus

Time type: Full time

Posted on: Posted 30+ Days Ago

Job Requisition ID: R4042

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That's our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you're driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you're ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

JPL is unique among NASA Centers in that its staff are Caltech employees, yet can access NASA technical resources. Cross-discipline teamwork is standard here: colleagues across JPL's science and engineering organizations and on Caltech's academic campus often work together. Learning to speak and understand other disciplines' languages is a doorway to the creativity needed to do what has not been done before. JPL staff are encouraged to create mission concepts that address humanity's core questions through a combination of science and technology. They are supported in developing ideas into proposals and hardware, and in communicating funded missions' results to the scientific community and the broader public. JPL seeks to employ scientists and engineers who are passionate about lifelong learning and excited to both contribute to and lead team efforts. We emphasize the importance of partnering across discipline boundaries and creating a friendly, constructive work environment to overcome space exploration's challenges. The Postdoctoral scholars at JPL benefit from an informal mentoring network, an annual conference showcasing their results, a dedicated seminar series, exposure to diverse career paths, and social connections across the JPL and Caltech community for advice on housing, childcare, and other aspects of living in southern California.

The Microdevices Laboratory (MDL) of Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) was established 3 decades ago with the goal of providing capabilities for development of components, sensors, and instruments for the JPL/NASA space program. Since inception, MDL has enjoyed significant success in enabling new missions, new measurements, and ultimately new science for space. In order to maintain and excel the current leadership role, it is essential to identify and carry high quality research programs that are targeted toward future important scientific and technical goals of NASA and JPL utilizing the existing and expanding capabilities at MDL.

Our approach: hire a number of outstanding postdoc researchers to focus on long term technology development in the areas of:

- Integrated Optics

- Nano-photonics

- Quantum sensors

- Space detectors

- Sensors and microsystems for harsh environment lidars, radars, and spectrometers

- New microfabrication processes for disruptive microdevice technologies

We currently have several open positions for outstanding postdoc researchers to define and develop microdevices technologies, components, and subsystems at MDL. Future microdevices developed at MDL will be critical for future NASA/JPL missions, with a focus on the 2025 and 2035 timeframes. The appointee(s) will carry out research in collaboration with the JPL advisor(s), resulting in publications in the open literature.

Job Requirements:

- Ph.D. or equivalent experience in engineering

- Substantial hands-on experience in micro-/nanofabrication and cleanroom processes

- In-depth knowledge of advanced lithographic techniques, DRIE, thin-film deposition

- Strong publication record demonstrating original thinking, and ability to conduct research both independently, and collaboratively

- Effective written and oral communication skills

Applicants may be subject to additional program requirements by NASA. Postdoctoral Scholar positions are awarded for a minimum of one-year period and may be renewed up to a maximum of three years. Candidates should submit the following to this site: CV, representative publications, contact information for three references, and a cover letter stating their research accomplishments and interests.

JPL has a catalog of benefits and perks that span from the traditional to the unique. This includes a variety of health, dental, vision, wellbeing, and retirement plans, paid time off, learning, rideshare, childcare, flexible schedule, parental leave and many more. Our focus is on work-life balance, and living healthy, fulfilling lives as we Dare Mighty Things Together. For benefits eligible positions, benefits are effective the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following the employee's start date.

For further benefits information click Benefits and Perks

The hiring range displayed below is specifically for those who will work in or reside in the location listed. In extending an offer, Jet Propulsion Laboratory considers factors including, but not limited to, the candidate's job related skills, experience, knowledge, and relevant education/training. Hiring range for this job may be adjusted based on primary work location outside of Pasadena, California. This adjusted range will be provided to candidates by the Recruiter when applicable.

The typical full time equivalent annual hiring range for this job in Pasadena, California: $82,180 - $82,180.

JPL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, religion, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy or perceived pregnancy, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, protected military or veteran status or any other characteristic or condition protected by Federal, state or local law.

In addition, JPL is a VEVRAA Federal Contractor.

About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

Wellington Management is seeking motivated undergraduate students to join our 2027 Technology Summer Internship Program. This 10-week paid internship provides hands-on software engineering experience, mentorship, and exposure to the investment management industry and the technologies that support it.

Technology plays a critical role in enabling Wellington's investment, business, and client teams. Our technologist's partner with teams across the firm to build innovative solutions, improve decision-making, and support the needs of a global investment organization.

Interns will work full-time (40 hours/week) at our Boston headquarters beginning June 2027. Interns are eligible for a housing stipend and a flexible work model that includes four days per week in the office and one remote workday.

Designed for students from a variety of academic backgrounds, this program is intended for candidates with prior experience in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related technical field who want to apply those skills to building practical technology solutions. Interns will have the opportunity to explore career paths in Wellington’s technology organization and do meaningful work alongside experienced professionals.

What You'll Do

As a summer intern, you will work alongside a cohort of fellow interns on a summer-long project focused on building a software solution that addresses a real business challenge at Wellington. Working as part of a project team, you'll gain hands-on experience in software engineering, data analysis, and product-oriented problem solving while developing technical, professional, and leadership skills.

Summer Project Experience

- Collaborate with fellow interns to identify, design, build, test and deliver a software application that addresses a real business challenge facing Wellington.

- Analyze user needs, gather feedback, and apply creative problem-solving to develop solutions that drive meaningful business impact.

- Gain hands-on experience applying software engineering and data analysis skills, including requirements gathering, application design, coding, testing, user feedback, and iterative delivery.

- Take ownership of a key project workstream while partnering closely with teammates and stakeholders to achieve shared goals.

- Build relationships across the firm through networking, collaboration, and engagement with business and technology professionals.

- Present project outcomes, recommendations, and lessons learned to senior leaders at the conclusion of the program.

- Work on challenges that evolve each year to reflect changing business priorities, emerging technologies, and opportunities for innovation.

What You'll Gain

Throughout the program, interns will:

- Gain exposure to the intersection of technology, business, and investment management within a global asset management firm.

- Experience how diverse technology disciplines work together to solve complex business challenges and deliver value for clients and colleagues.

- Develop technical, analytical, and professional skills through hands-on experience, mentorship and real-world project work.

- Build meaningful relationships with leaders, professionals, and fellow interns across the firm.

- Strengthen communication, collaboration, leadership, and problem-solving skills in a supportive and team-oriented way.

- Gain confidence presenting ideas, influencing stakeholders and translating complex concepts into actionable recommendations.

- Explore potential career paths within technology while developing a deeper understanding of Wellington’s culture and business.

Who Should Apply

We welcome students from a broad range of majors, backgrounds, experiences, and academic disciplines. Candidates should have experience applying technical skills through coursework, internships, research, independent projects, or other hands-on work in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related field.

We look for:

- Current sophomore or junior undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor's degree.

- Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

- Experience with software engineering, data analysis, or a related technical field, including familiarity with at least one programming language such as Python.

- Involvement in campus organizations, leadership activities, volunteer work, or other extracurricular experiences.

- Ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.

- No prior finance experience is required.

- Curious and adaptable in exploring emerging technologies and AI tools in your work, school, and projects

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Application Deadline: October 2, 2026

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds.

As an equal opportunity employer, Wellington Management ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, creed, national origin, age, ancestry, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, citizenship, marital status, pregnancy, veteran or military status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you are a candidate with a disability, or are assisting a candidate with a disability, and require an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please email us at GMWTalentOperations@wellington.com.

At Wellington Management, our approach to compensation is designed to help us attract, inspire and retain the best talent in our industry. We strive to pay employees fairly and competitively across all levels and roles. Our approach to compensation considers all aspects of total compensation; all employees are eligible to receive salary, variable compensation, and benefits. The base salary range for this position is:

$19-$35 per hour

This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education. This range is an estimate, and further details on salary and total compensation aspects will be shared with candidates during the recruitment process.

Base salary is only one component of Wellington’s total compensation approach. Other rewards may include a discretionary Corporate Bonus and/ or Incentives, if eligible. In addition, we offer a comprehensive and high value benefit package to meet the unique needs of our employees and their families, and we are committed to fostering a flexible work environment that enables employees to thrive personally and professionally. Examples of our benefits include retirement plan, health and wellbeing, dental, vision, and pharmacy coverage, health savings account, flexible spending accounts and commuter program, employee assistance program, life and disability insurance, adoption assistance, back-up childcare, tuition/CFA reimbursement and paid time off (leave of absence, paid holidays, volunteer, sick and vacation time)

We believe that in person interactions inspire and energize our community and are essential to our culture. In support of this commitment, our employees work from our offices 4 days a week with flexibility to work remotely 1 day a week. We believe that this approach ultimately supports our mission to deliver investment excellence to our clients and their beneficiaries over the long term.

The Opportunity

Adobe is seeking dedicated and curious Software Engineer interns to help design, build, and evolve the systems that power our products and platforms.

As an intern, you’ll work in an AI-enabled development environment, where modern tools accelerate how software is built and tested. You’ll collaborate with experienced engineers and multi-functional partners, including designers and product managers, to contribute to real-world systems while continuing to build your technical and problem-solving skills.

Software engineering opportunities at Adobe span a broad range of products, technologies, and technical problem spaces. Whether you're passionate about creating intuitive user experiences, building scalable systems, or solving complex engineering challenges, we'll consider your technical skills, interests, and team needs when identifying the best opportunity within our engineering organization.

This role is designed for early-career engineers who are excited not only about writing code, but also about understanding how software works end-to-end, validating solutions, and connecting technical decisions to real user and product outcomes.

All 2027 Adobe interns will be co-located hybrid. This means that interns will work between their assigned office and home. Interns will be based in the office where their manager and/or team are located, where they will get the most support to ensure collaboration and the best employee experience. Managers and their organization will determine the frequency they need to go into the office to meet priorities.

What You’ll Do

- Develop high-quality, reliable, testable, and maintainable code using modern engineering practices

- Contribute to all phases of the software development lifecycle, including design, implementation, testing, debugging, and documentation

- Work with AI-assisted development tools to support coding, testing, and debugging, while learning how to validate outputs for correctness and quality

- Review and improve code ensuring performance, scalability, and maintainability

- Collaborate with engineers through stand-ups, code reviews, and design discussions

- Contribute to solution design and help improve product quality, reliability, and performance with guidance from experienced engineers

- Solve issues, debug problems, and iterate on solutions in a fast-paced environment

- Communicate clearly and effectively with teammates, sharing ideas, asking questions, and incorporating feedback

- Grow your technical and professional skills while contributing to a positive, inclusive engineering culture

What You Need to Succeed

- Enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s academic program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, with graduation between December 2027 - June 2028

- Strong foundation in software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and coding principles

- Experience through coursework, personal projects, or internships building applications or systems

- Proficiency in at least one programming language such as Java, Python, C++, or JavaScript

- Familiarity with the software development lifecycle - designing, building, deploying, and maintaining applications

- Exposure to or interest in modern development tools, including AI-assisted tools, and an understanding of how to use them responsibly

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to debug and reason through technical challenges

- Ability to learn quickly, adapt to new technologies, and take initiative in solving problems

- Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively within a team

- Ability to participate in a full-time internship between May-September

About Adobe

Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. About Us

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience: Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you’re in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast.

Are you the person who takes the product apart to see how it works, then redesigns it in your head? Do you want to know why people buy what they buy — and then go build the thing they didn’t know they needed? Are you excited by the challenge of turning an insight into a product that lands in millions of homes? If so, we invite you to learn more about Product Development, Design & Consumer Insights Co-op opportunities at SharkNinja.

This is a single application for product development, design, and consumer insights early talent roles across SharkNinja. The hiring teams are spread across our product development, industrial and experience design, culinary, consumer insights, and consumer experience functions.

Whichever team you join, you’ll work on real products and real launches alongside people who have shipped them before. You might be sketching a concept that becomes a hero product, specifying the exact color and finish a consumer sees on the shelf, running usability sessions on a connected app, testing recipes to prove out what an appliance can really do, digging into field feedback to close a consumer pain point, or synthesizing research into the recommendation that changes a product’s direction. If you’re curious, consumer-obsessed, hands-on, and ready to make an impact from day one, we want to hear from you!

Teams that you can be connected to through this posting include:

- Product Development (Shark, Ninja, and Beauty)

- Ninja Test Kitchen / Culinary Development

- Industrial Design

- CMF (Color, Material & Finish) Design

- UX/UI Design

- Consumer Insights

- Customer Experience & Product Support

Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:

- Contribute to real product launches across Shark, Ninja, and Beauty, from early research and concepting through to shelf

- Translate consumer insights into product and design decisions that shape what actually gets built

- Bring ideas to life through sketches, renderings, prototypes, wireframes, and design specifications

- Conduct hands-on product testing and competitive research, and document findings that influence design direction

- Present your work and the thinking behind it to cross-functional partners and design leads — and incorporate their feedback

- Collaborate across Product Development, Industrial Design, Engineering, Marketing, Consumer Insights, and Product Management

- Gain exposure to the full product development cycle, solving simultaneously for performance, cost, and delight

- Own a meaningful project end to end and present your contributions to SharkNinja leaders

Depending on the team, your day-to-day may include:

Product Development, Insights & Consumer Experience

- Developing user-relevant design targets for product performance and user experience — human factors, touchpoints, KPIs, and Consumer Satisfaction Indicators — and championing them to engineers, industrial designers, and commercial marketers

- Acting as a product “expert” for cross-functional questions, and assisting with new product setups, product information management, and competitive landscape development

- Supporting qualitative and quantitative research, designing and refining research tools such as surveys and discussion guides, and translating unmet and latent needs into clear recommendations for new products and features

- Building customer personas and journey maps, identifying whitespace opportunities and consumer pain points, and monitoring competitors and market trends to inform positioning

- Supporting the post-purchase consumer journey — replacement component specifications, self-service content, and consumer-facing artwork assets

- Culinary testing and hero recipe development alongside food scientists and research chefs, evaluating performance and quality for launches such as the Ninja Creami, Crispi, and Luxe Café

- Recording test results accurately and synthesizing insights into stories that influence brand, product, and executive strategy

Industrial, CMF & Digital Experience Design

- Translating consumer insights into bold, user-centered design solutions through sketches, illustrations, and high-fidelity renderings

- Creating product designs in SolidWorks or Rhino, producing renderings in KeyShot, and collaborating with Engineering to deliver clean, production-ready CAD files

- Specifying the full look and feel of a product — surface finish, color, material, texture, and branding — and creating, tracking, and maintaining color specifications (ID SPECS)

- Developing color palette proposals targeted for different retailers, organizing supplier CMF samples into a material library, and working to standards such as Pantone, NCS, SPI, YickSang, and Mold-Tech

- Supporting UI design, icon design, and rating/warning label creation, and interacting daily with the APAC manufacturing team, suppliers, and the Compliance team

- Creating wireframes, interactive prototypes, and visual design specs in Figma, Adobe XD, or Sketch for mobile app and embedded UI experiences

- Participating in usability testing, maintaining and evolving design systems for cross-platform consistency, and designing for accessibility, responsiveness, and internationalization

- Building visual and functional prototypes, and exploring emerging trends, new materials, and future-forward aesthetics

ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:

- Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s or PhD program or has graduated from such a program within the past year — Industrial Design, Product Design, UX/UI or Interaction Design, Mechanical Engineering, Marketing, Market Research, Psychology or Sociology, Culinary Arts or Food Science, Business, Communications, or similar

- Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week onsite-hybrid schedule; specific location and number of onsite days vary by team and term

- A consumer-first perspective and real curiosity about how people actually use products in their homes

- Strong visual and verbal storytelling — you can present an idea, explain the thinking behind it, and take feedback well

Job Description

The Role

General Motors is seeking a curious, analytical, and collaborative graduate student to join the Global Customer Research team for Summer 2027. This project-based internship offers hands-on experience using customer and market research to help inform business decisions across General Motors.

As a Global Customer Research Intern, you will support research projects from planning through delivery, analyze customer and market information, and translate findings into clear insights and recommendations. You will work alongside experienced researchers and internal partners to understand customer behavior, identify meaningful themes, and communicate what the findings mean for the business.

This internship is an opportunity to build experience in both quantitative and qualitative research, supplier management, data analysis, storytelling, and executive communication while helping General Motors keep the customer at the center of its decisions.

The Team

The Global Customer Research team helps General Motors understand the people, markets, and behaviors that shape customer decisions. The team gathers, analyzes, and synthesizes the voice of the customer to provide insights that inform business strategy, product development, marketing, and the overall customer experience.

The team partners with leaders and stakeholders across Brand, Product, Marketing, Planning, Program Management, Engineering, and Design. It also works with external research suppliers to design and deliver studies that answer important business questions. As an intern, you will learn from research managers and collaborate with internal and external partners in a supportive, project-focused environment.

What You’ll Do

- Manage research projects and suppliers from beginning to end; holding to time and budget targets.

- Collect, review, and analyze market research results; identify key insights from data analysis and recommend appropriate course of action.

- Consult with internal stakeholders to frame the specific learning objectives for primary research, and work alongside the research manager to apply appropriate research methodologies that will best fulfill the goal.

- Provide internal teams with consumer and market insights – including: Brand Teams, Product Teams, Marketing, Planning, Program Management, Engineering, and Design.

- Develop and deliver effective presentations to inform business decisions and strategic initiatives to multiple GM leadership levels and organizations.

- Develop quantitative questionnaires and qualitative discussion guides.

- Conduct special analyses utilizing current data or industry trends to further enhance the research findings.

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Master's or MBA degree in market research, business administration, economics, statistics, industrial-organizational psychology, or a related field.

- Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028.

- Available to work full time (40 hours per week) during the internship.

- Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

- Curiosity about people, markets, and the “why” behind customer behavior.

- Willingness to learn, ask thoughtful questions, take initiative, and contribute in a collaborative team environment.

- Foundational analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to organize information, identify themes, and communicate clear takeaways.

- Ability to manage assigned work, meet deadlines, and stay organized across multiple priorities with guidance from the research team.

- Ability to work effectively with teammates, internal stakeholders, and external suppliers.

- Foundational ability to use AI-enabled tools for prompt engineering, building and using productivity agents, and drafting, editing, and refining professional documents.

Preferred Qualifications

- Curiosity to understand the “why” behind the data and translate findings into clear implications.

- Proficiency with Google Workspace, including Slides, Docs, and Sheets.

- Hands-on experience using AI-enabled tools for data analysis and visualization.

- Experience evaluating AI-generated outputs for accuracy, quality, bias, traceability, and fitness for purpose.

- Experience using Qualtrics, including survey programming, JavaScript, Stats iQ, and XM Directory.

- Familiarity with statistical concepts and applications.

- Familiarity with quantitative and qualitative market research methods, including conjoint analysis and MaxDiff.

Position Description

Our Company's Research Lab’s Robotics and Workflow Data Capture (WDC) teams develop automated laboratory systems and digital technologies that allow scientists to generate high-quality research data efficiently and reliably. By combining laboratory automation with software solutions that capture, organize, and analyze scientific data, these teams reduce manual processes, improve workflow efficiency, and support research across multiple sites. Their work plays a critical role in accelerating scientific discovery and advancing the development of new medicines.

The successful candidate will contribute to innovative projects focused on artificial intelligence, software development, and laboratory automation, helping to improve how automation workflows are created, documented, and supported across research sites. This internship provides an opportunity to work alongside automation engineers and data scientists while gaining hands-on experience with AI/LLM technologies, GitHub, programming, data analytics, and laboratory automation systems. The project will have a lasting impact by improving knowledge sharing, troubleshooting capabilities, and automation standardization across scientific laboratories.

Overview
The intern will support a cross-functional initiative between the Robotics and Workflow Data Capture teams focused on improving how laboratory automation software is developed, documented, and supported across research laboratories. The project will leverage programming, AI/LLM technologies, GitHub repositories, and automation data to develop an AI-enabled knowledge platform that helps scientists and engineers understand automation scripts, troubleshoot issues, and follow standardized scripting practices. The intern's work will contribute to improved knowledge sharing, faster problem resolution, enhanced onboarding, and greater consistency in automation workflows across sites.

- Collaborate with automation scientists and data science professionals across Robotics and Workflow Data Capture teams, as well as our cross-site scientific partners in Boston and South San Francisco.

- Develop and evaluate an AI-enabled knowledge repository that supports automation script understanding, troubleshooting, and workflow development.

- Support integration of GitHub repositories, technical documentation, and automation records into a centralized knowledge platform

- Assist in developing and optimizing tools and processes to improve automation error tracking, analysis, and resolution.

- Create user guidance, technical documentation, and standardized best practices to support automation workflow scripting development and knowledge transfer

- Prepare technical summaries and presentations of project findings.

- Related scientific discipline

- Strong Python and SQL programming skills, especially toward developing scripts, APIs, or lightweight applications

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

About Dexmate

Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. Our mission is to democratize robotics by lowering the barrier to entry, delivering a plug-and-play platform for developers, researchers, and enterprises, and cultivating an open ecosystem that accelerates the evolution of physical AI.

If you want to help shape the next layer of human capability — and believe the future of robotics should be built together, not in isolation — we'd love to build it with you.

The Role

We are looking for PhD research interns to push the frontier of robot learning on real hardware. You will develop new algorithms for dexterous manipulation, navigation, and control, train and fine-tune large models, and validate your ideas on Dexmate robots alongside our research and engineering teams.

Responsibilities

- Develop new algorithms and methods for training AI models for enhancing the robot dexterity.

- Conduct cutting edge research across multiple disciplines (Robotics, RL/IL, control, perception, LLM, VLM, etc.).

- Work with large-scale ML systems and large-scale model training/fine-tuning.

- Design and implement state-of-the-art learning-based manipulation/navigation/control algorithms on real robots.

- Work with other teams to develop a diverse set of robust manipulation skills for robots.

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a PhD degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, etc., or related technical field.

- Passionate about working with robots.

- Research experience in embodied AI, robotics, computer vision, machine learning, human-AI interaction, and computer science.

- Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

- Must obtain work authorization in U.S. at the time of hire and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment.

- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

- At least 2 years of experience conducting independent research.

- Deep understanding of the SOTA robot learning techniques (reinforcement learning, imitation learning, etc.)

This role will partner with cross-functional business, technology, and functional leaders to prioritize a portfolio of opportunities, build the business case for each, and support the hands-on design and configuration of solutions. The Role

We are looking for a highly motivated Data & Business Analyst Intern to join Schonfeld’s Systematic Strategies COO (SCOO) team.

The Systematic business contains many separate investment (PM) teams. Schonfeld oversees these teams’ trading and risk, and supports them with capital, technology, execution, operations, legal, recruiting and general business services (aka the Platform). The SCOO team is the key interface between PM teams and these services.

Working within the SCOO team, you will build, enhance, and automate the tools and analytics used by our Platform to make faster data-driven decisions at scale.

This internship blends data, technology, and markets: you will gain exposure to systematic trading workflows, enterprise data architecture, AI/LLM development, and cross-functional project management while solving real operational challenges.

What You’ll Do

- Investigate and integrate multiple enterprise data sources to build a unified analytics library for the SCOO team, handling diverse endpoints (PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Kafka streams)

- Design and deploy AI-assisted data tools using agent skills and Python libraries that enable non-technical stakeholders to query complex data through natural language

- Build production dashboards and automated reports (Power BI, Grafana, or HTML) that surface trading activity, vendor relationships, execution analytics, and operational KPIs

- Automate manual processes including quarterly updates, onboarding tracking, expense reconciliation, and other tasks that require recurring data pulls using orchestration frameworks such as Prefect and Airflow

- Collaborate across Technology, Risk, Operations, Reference Data, and Execution Services teams to understand data schemas, navigate access permissions, and validate data quality across systems

- Create scripts and schemas for ad-hoc analyses (e.g., “How has average FX ticket size changed over time?”).

- Document processes and proactively surface ideas to improve efficiency, data quality, and transparency across the Platform

What You’ll Bring

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Finance, or a related quantitative field (with ≤ 1 year left in your program).

- Proficient in Python (Pandas, FastAPI/Flask, OOP) and SQL (query optimization, data modelling) - able to deliver rapid ad-hoc analyses and scale them into production-ready tools within the broader tech stack

- AI/LLM tool development experience or strong interest; experience with agent skills, MCP servers, or RAG systems is a plus

- Rapid learning ability and comfort with ambiguity - you'll need to quickly understand unfamiliar systems by reading technical docs, talking to engineers, and experimenting

- Hands-on experience in dashboard development (Power BI, Grafana, HTML) and knowledge of workflow orchestration tools (Prefect, Airflow, Dagster)

- Genuine interest in understanding how systematic trading works - execution flows, broker relationships, business operations, and the data that supports decision-making

- Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders

- Comfort working autonomously in a fast-paced, global, highly collaborative environment

Our Internship

Kick-start your career in finance with the Schonfeld Summer Internship! Over the course of 10 action-packed weeks, you will have the opportunity to build solutions that tackle real-world challenges and leave a lasting impact on the firm. As an intern, you’ll join a close-knit team that is ready to support your growth and accelerate your career. We will pair you with a dedicated manager and a mentor who’ll guide your development over the course of the internship and beyond. Throughout the program, you will have the chance to connect with senior leaders through a series of learning sessions, attend hands-on skills workshops, network at social events and get a behind-the-scenes look at how various functions power the firm. We’ll empower you to bring your ideas to life and make an impact.

Who We Are

Schonfeld is a global multi-manager hedge fund that strives to deliver industry-leading risk-adjusted returns for our investors. We leverage both internal and external portfolio manager teams around the world, seeking to capitalize on inefficiencies and opportunities within the markets. We draw from decades of experience and a significant investment in proprietary technology, infrastructure and risk analytics to invest across four main strategies: Quant, Tactical, Fundamental Equity and Discretionary Macro & Fixed Income.

Our Culture

At Schonfeld, we’ll invest in you. Attracting and retaining top talent is at the heart of what we do, because we believe that exceptional outcomes begin with exceptional people. We foster a culture where talent is empowered to continually learn, innovate and pursue ambitious goals. We are teamwork-oriented, collaborative and encourage ideas—at all levels—to be shared. As an organization committed to investing in our people, we provide learning and educational offerings and opportunities to make an impact. We encourage community through internal networks, external partnerships and service initiatives that promote inclusion and purpose beyond the firm’s walls.

Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

Advancing the World’s Technology Together

Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities.

What You’ll Learn

- Project Overview: AI memory is now the bottleneck of AI systems: power and heat decide how fast models can run. Our lab turns RTL and trace behavior into time-indexed power models that drive a trace-driven power and thermal simulator.

- Skills You’ll Learn:

- Power macromodeling

- RTL and SystemC power feature extraction

- Trace-driven power and thermal simulation

What You’ll Do

Samsung’s Power & Thermal Lab is seeking an RTL focused intern to help build and validate the power models that the simulator runs on real AI memory components.

We are a small, fast‑moving team where direct ownership and minimal busywork empower every member to tackle the same real‑world problems. Working with authentic data, real partners, and production‑grade results, our contributions flow straight into platforms used across the company.

As an intern, you will support research and product teams across multiple projects, including creating and validating IP‑level power macromodels for AI‑memory components. You will work on real projects with tangible results, receive mentorship, and help shape the scope of work in a collaborative environment where hardware, software, and thermal experts work side‑by‑side on next‑generation AI memory technologies.

Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy

Reports to: SVP, R&D (Power & Thermal Lab)

- Develop IP-level power macromodels for AI memory components such as PHY, memory controller, interconnect, and TSV, using analytical models, lookup tables, FSM, neural networks, and their hybrids.

- Extract activity, value, and state dependent power features from RTL, SystemC, and C simulations.

- Support calibration with synthesis assisted anchors, circuit level references, and measured data.

- Validate your models against RTL and gate level power analysis and silicon, and improve them where they disagree.

- Deliver validated models and regression checks into the trace-driven flow, working with the software engineers on model interfaces.

- Complete other responsibilities as assigned.

What You Bring

- MS or PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

- Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining.

- RTL design and analysis experience (Verilog, SystemVerilog, SystemC), and solid C++ or Python.

- Understanding of dynamic and leakage power in CMOS and interconnect, and the ability to abstract circuit behavior into compact models.

- Curiosity about power, heat, and AI hardware; you like to measure rather than guess.

- Experience with power analysis tools such as PrimeTime PX, StarRC, VCS, or PowerArtist, architecture level modeling tools such as McPAT, CACTI, or Wattch, S-parameters and SPICE, UCIe or high speed I/O or 2.5D packaging, preferred

- You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people.

- An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding.

- You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches.

- Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change.

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Overview: Before a single transistor gets placed, someone has to decide what the chip should actually be and ensure it functions to specs. This team makes those calls including System on a Chip (SoC) -level architecture, fabric/interconnect design, verification and not just core compute.

What you might work on: This posting spans multiple teams within Hardware Architecture & AI Hardware and SoC . One application, one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team and location that fits best. What each team does:

- Architecture: We define and evaluate the system, CPU, memory, fabric, and chiplet-level decisions that shape future products. We analyze workloads, performance, power, and system requirements, develop architectural models, do tradeoff analyses, and specifications for implementation.

- AI Hardware: We design and develop the core AI accelerator IP, including compute, data movement, and other specialized hardware blocks that enable high-performance AI workloads. We take these IPs from requirements through RTL design, verification, and delivery for SoC integration.

- SOC : Our team is where everything comes together. We design and verify the integration of all subsystems and the final pieces that allow the chip to interact with the outside world; scaleout, memory and on-chip system management and security. We validate cross functional and performance requirements, and ultimately take the design to silicon.

This role is on-site, based out of Boston, MA or Austin, TX or Fort Collins, CO or Santa Clara, CA.

Who You Are

- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, ECE, CE, or CS.

- Coursework or projects in digital design, computer architecture and performance modeling.

- Self-starter who brings sound judgment and practical problem-solving to every project with a solid interest in AI and hardware, along with the ability to take ownership and deliver results.

What We Need

- Familiarity with ASIC design concepts, ranging from performance simulations, RTL design / verification, and logic synthesis / timing analysis

- Scripting & programming skills (example: Python, PERL, tcl, C/C++); with experience using AI coding platforms

- [Architecture] Experience with architectural simulators.

- Exposure to RISC-V or other open ISAs is nice to have.

- FPGA design experience is nice to have.

What You Will Learn

- Taking designs from specification to RTL to verification, and learning the qualification checks and tools needed to do so.

- How architectural tradeoffs (Architecture: Compute vs. memory vs. interconnect. AI HW/ SOC: Power, Performance & Area) get decided with data, not intuition.

- Best practices for cross-functional collaboration, seeing firsthand how Architecture, RTL, Software, and Physical Design teams stay aligned through implementation.

- Practical methods to integrate AI tools directly into your daily technical workflow.

- [Architecture] Performance modeling methodology used before RTL existed.

USA Hiring Timelines

This internship opportunity is available throughout our 3 terms with the following corresponding recruitment cycles:

- Winter Term: Jan–Apr work term, Sept–Dec recruit.

- Summer Term: May–Aug work term, Oct–Apr recruit.

- Fall Term: Sept–Dec work term, Jan–Aug recruit.

AXQ Capital is a global quantitative investment firm. We build diverse sources of investment edge across geographies, asset classes, and trading horizons. Our strategies are grounded in rigorous scientific research and deep market understanding, strengthened by sustained investment in data, technology, and AI. Our team brings together exceptional talent from leading academic institutions and the world’s most respected quantitative firms. We foster a collaborative culture built on curiosity, rigor, and ownership, where the best ideas win and people grow with the firm.

Markets are noisy, competitive, and constantly evolving — finding a durable edge is one of the hardest problems in applied research. As a Quantitative Research Intern, you will take on that challenge directly. Over the course of your internship, you will work on one or two projects in areas such as:

- Developing and refining quantitative trading strategies under the guidance of experienced portfolio managers and researchers

- Applying tools from probability, statistics, and machine learning to uncover patterns and predictive signals in market data

- Leveraging agentic AI workflows to accelerate the research cycle — from hypothesis generation to automated backtesting and analysis

- Transforming raw, messy datasets into research-ready inputs that power alpha discovery

- Exploring portfolio construction and optimization techniques that combine individual strategies into robust, risk-managed portfolios

Qualifications

- Undergraduate or graduate student at a top-tier university in a quantitative field (e.g., mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, computer science, financial engineering)

- Strong foundation in probability and statistics, including statistical modeling, time-series analysis, and machine learning

- Proficient in Python for data analysis and research

- Intellectually curious and quick to learn, with a genuine interest in quantitative finance

- Clear communicator who works well in a team and under pressure

We’d Love It If You Have

- Publications in leading academic journals or conferences

- Strong results in national or international Olympiads (math, physics, or computer science)

This role is open year-round. We welcome applications for full-time internships during academic breaks as well as part-time roles during the academic year, based in our New York office. Early Career Talent @ Perplexity

​Perplexity believes that exceptionally talented individuals at any stage can thrive in our high-velocity, high-ownership culture. ​Our early career talent program revolves around:

- ​Breadth: New grads at Perplexity work across the stack, from Perplexity's agent harnesses to our AI inference and training systems. Many of our most beloved features and most important systems were shipped by individuals fresh out of school.

- ​Depth: New grads are entrusted (and expected) to dive deep into whatever problem domains you work on. Often, your work will require you to become a world expert in some problem space that few others in the world have encountered.

- ​Recognition: We select for the best and we recognize them accordingly. We set our early career compensation to rise well above that of top tech companies and startups. Post-hire, we aggressively recognize and reward growth in role.

A Foundational Company

Rilla is on a mission to index the offline world.

Today, we’ve built the leading sales coaching software for organizations doing sales offline. We have over 1000 customers, including The Home Depot, KKR, Neighborly, and PulteGroup, using our product to enable AI sales coaching across their organization.

We are backed by Google Ventures, Bessemer Ventures, Crew Capital, and Broom Ventures, along with others.

We’re an in office team in NYC with builders who operate like high speed reinforcement learners. We obsess over our customers, move at a high velocity, are not afraid of failure, and look to maximize our real-world impact.

If you want to build the products and systems for how billions of conversations in the real world are captured and indexed, Rilla is the place to do it.

The Role

Rilla engineers architect and ship features across the stack at lightning speed. On a daily basis, you will build end-to-end workflows, take them to production, and solve real world problems across an out-sized scale.

As an early technical steward, you will raise the bar for code quality and decision‑making, setting patterns that cement a world‑class engineering culture as we scale. While the company 10×’s, your scope and ownership will grow just as fast—building the tools, mental models, and platforms that let both you and Rilla accelerate exponentially.

Do you describe yourself as "obsessive"? Do you aspire to be a founder or a leader in applying AI to the physical world? We believe Rilla is the best place — with the best peers — to learn how.

Technologies We Use

- Different languages and frameworks, including React, React Native, Typescript and Python

- Open-source technologies like Node.js, PostgreSQL, Turborepo, Lodash, and Zod

- Industry-standard build tooling, including GitHub Actions, Terraform, and Spacelift

What We Value

- An infinite learner. Someone who is relentless in their curiosity.

- A customer obsessive. Someone who deeply care about delighting customers and solving real pains, not vanity metrics.

- A winning attitude. You thrive with extreme accountability, learning as a team, and both giving and receiving rapid feedback.

- Extreme empathy. Our customers are not tech companies. They live and work in the real world. Empathy is critical to arriving at correct solutions.

- Unafraid of failure. You take risks. You see failure as an opportunity to learn, grow, and be better the next time. In a weird way, you trick your brain into being excited when you fail, because it means you got a new opportunity to learn more.

What We Require

- Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Javascript, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages.

- Strong engineering prowess, ideally developed at start-ups.

- Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality.

Don’t Work Here

Please don't join if you're not excited about:

- Building an AI product for an industry untouched by modern software

- Constantly talking to and visiting customers in the field

- Working ~60 hrs/week in person with some of the most ambitious people in NYC

- Attempting to build a generational company, and the intensity required to do so

- Breakfast, lunch, dinner, and supplementary food and drink — 6x a week

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. As one of the largest global security companies in the world, Northrop Grumman is proud to help our nation’s military personnel make the transition to civilian careers. Approximately 1/4th of Northrop Grumman’s 90,000 employees self-identifies as veterans, and more than 1,600 are reservists. The Northrop Grumman Military Internship Program (NG-MIP) is an approved SkillBridge Program under Dept. of Defense Instruction 1322.29. The NG-MIP program is an opportunity for transitioning service members to gain valuable civilian work experience through an individual internship during their last 6 months of service, for up to 180 days. The Northrop Grumman Military Internship Program is open to all ranks and experience levels. SkillBridge participants are not eligible for compensation from Northrop Grumman, as they continue to receive military compensation and benefits as Active-duty service members.

Responsibilities for this internship position are:

Northrop Grumman Corporation (NGC) has developed the Northrop Grumman – Military Internship Program (DoD SkillBridge) utilizing the DoDI guidance for Skillbridge. During this program the service member will be on-site at his or her host company performing an individual internship in an entry to mid-level career type role. The service member will be on the job training supporting a work schedule equivalent to 40hrs per week. Outlined below are the Goals, Objectives, and Outcomes for the program.

Goals – Provide transitioning service members fellowship-style job skills training during the last portion(s) of their military commitment. This program is specifically designed to offer internships that result in the potential to transition to a full-time opportunity as the conclusion of the training. Interns will serve as a pipeline for high-speed, motivated military candidates into NGC.

Objectives - Service Members who complete the Intern program will be highly trained, capable, future employees that align to the specific needs of the organization and are prepared to meet the NG mission “Defining Possible” on Day 1. This program provides a comprehensive internship experience including professional development, networking with leadership, and training specifically focused on NG leadership principles, company history, customer/stakeholder engagement, product and service overview, and core job responsibilities.

Outcome – Offer transitioning service member a rewarding opportunity to join the Northrop Grumman team.

DoD SkillBridge Eligibility:

- Has served at least 180 days on active duty
- Is within 12 months of separation or retirement
- Will receive an honorable discharge
- Has taken any service TAPS/TGPS
- Has attended or participated in an ethics brief within the last 12 months
- Received Unit Commander (first O-4/Field Grade commander in chain of command) written authorization and approval to participate in DoD SkillBridge Program prior to start of internship.

GCCS-J is the Department of Defense (DoD) Joint Command and Control (C2) system of record. GCCS-J supports commanders and warfighters as they conduct joint and multinational operations by providing a fused picture of the battlespace within an integrated system that supports Joint Warfighter needs today. The program's Intelligence product area is focused on improving how intelligence data is integrated, analyzed, displayed, and operationalized across the GCCS-J modernization effort, enabling faster and better-informed decisions for mission leaders and joint operators.

This SkillBridge Intelligence Analyst role will collect, interpret, and transform raw operational, geospatial, and threat-related information into actionable intelligence while helping guide the development and modernization of intelligence capabilities within GCCS-J. The ideal candidate is disciplined, security-focused, operationally credible, and able to translate real-world mission needs into clear recommendations for leadership and technical teams.

Core Roles:

· Data Collector - Gather and organize intelligence from reports, imagery, message traffic, communications, operational data, and other relevant sources.

· Threat Assessor - Analyze adversary capabilities, patterns, movements, and intent to identify risks, support warning functions, and anticipate likely courses of action.

· Briefing Specialist - Convert complex operational and intelligence information into clear, concise products for commanders, program leadership, and engineering teams.

· Mission-to-Product Translator - Help guide GCCS-J modernization by translating analyst workflows, operational requirements, and mission pain points into inputs for product owners, systems engineers, developers, and testers.

Key Responsibilities:

· Collect, review, and assess intelligence from multiple sources, including reports, imagery, maps, historical records, operational data, and message traffic.

· Research targets, threat networks, operational environments, and adversary patterns to support situational awareness and mission planning.

· Monitor threat activity, communications, and movement trends to identify relevant indicators, anomalies, and emerging risks.

· Produce intelligence summaries, threat assessments, decision-support products, daily reports, and time-sensitive warning updates for leadership and mission stakeholders.

· Answer high-priority requests for information from commanders, program leaders, engineers, and other mission partners.

· Brief complex intelligence findings in a concise, decision-focused manner to both technical and non-technical audiences.

· Support GCCS-J intelligence capability development by identifying user needs, analyst workflows, data gaps, and operational pain points.

· Translate mission requirements into clear recommendations, candidate features, user stories, acceptance considerations, or workflow improvements for GCCS-J modernization teams.

· Collaborate with product owners, systems engineers, software engineers, and test teams to ensure intelligence-related capabilities align with operational realities and user expectations.

· Participate in demonstrations, reviews, and feedback sessions to validate that intelligence tools, data flows, and operational outputs support real-world mission use.

· Help evaluate how intelligence data sources and analyst functions integrate into GCCS-J command and control workflows across the Intelligence product area.

· Maintain strict adherence to classification guidance, security procedures, information handling rules, and operational protocols.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

· Current or recent military experience in any aspects of All-source intelligence “HUMINT, MASINT, SIGINT, GEOINT, IMINT, OSINT, TECHINT”, Targeting and Operational Mission Planning.

· Strong analytical thinking with the ability to evaluate incomplete, conflicting, or time-sensitive information and produce sound assessments.

· Ability to transform raw information into actionable intelligence products for operational or leadership use.

· Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write reports and deliver clear, concise briefings.

· Working knowledge of intelligence processes, military reporting, threat analysis, and support to command and control operations.

· Ability to translate operational problems, analyst needs, and mission workflows into structured recommendations for technical teams.

· Ability to work in a disciplined, high-accountability, mission-focused environment with minimal supervision.

· Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy under pressure.

· Ability to collaborate effectively with operational users, leadership, and cross-functional development teams.

· Understanding of security protocols, classified handling procedures, and information protection requirements.

· US citizen with a final Secret clearance.

· Meets DoD SkillBridge qualifications as per DoDI 1322.29.

Preferred Qualifications:

· Active Top Secret / SCI clearance or eligibility.

· Experience with GCCS-J, Joint C2 systems, Combatant Command operations, or intelligence support to command and control environments.

· Experience briefing senior leaders and turning complex intelligence into decision-focused recommendations.

· Familiarity with intelligence data integration, ISR workflows, imagery exploitation, or analyst support tools used in DoD environments.

· Exposure to Agile, DevSecOps, product development, backlog refinement, user feedback, or operational test and evaluation activities.

· Ability to work effectively with geographically dispersed mission and engineering teams in a modernization environment.

Primary Level Salary Range: $129,300.00 - $193,900.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

- Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

- Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

NYC Pay Transparency

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. About the team
Our team's mission is to empower genAI and content understanding in TikTok businesses. Computer vision and natural language processing are important dimensions in both content generation and understanding. We are working on various foundational models, including multi-modality pretraining, multi-modal large language model, image generation, video generation etc. As a genAI team on the business side, we try to succeed in both achieving business metric gains (recommendation metrics), and also producing state-of-the-art research outputs.

Project Overview, Challenges & Value
We aim to integrate recommendation large models multimodal large models, and the Agentic Rec framework to fundamentally reshape the underlying content distribution logic, empowering the system with deep semantic association and autonomous planning capabilities, exploring new frontiers in algorithmic design.

1. Recommendation Large Models: Address challenges such as gradient convergence and representation drift in ultra-long behavioral sequences, enabling the system to achieve true ""logical reasoning"" capabilities.
2. Unified Multimodal Semantic Space: Explore alignment across video, image-text content, and user intent, constructing a fully multimodal semantic space that goes beyond text.
3. Agentic Rec:Develop recommendation agents with capabilities such as self-reflection, tool invocation, and long-horizon planning, driving a transformation of recommendation and content distribution experiences.

Key challenges include:
1. Extreme-scale reasoning:
Performance gains and bottlenecks associated with ultra-large model parameters and ultra-long sequence modeling.
2. Multimodal fusion: Challenges in representation learning for cross-modal intent alignment.
3. Autonomous evolution: Breakthroughs in long-horizon planning and decision-making paradigms for agent systems.

Project Value:
1. Technical value: Explore new paradigms for recommendation, significantly improving recommendation performance and system efficiency.
2. Business value: Enable deeper understanding of user interests and content, improving distribution efficiency and enhancing satisfaction for both users and creators.
