- Design and develop next-generation large-scale recommendation systems optimized for personalized, engaging, and scalable user experiences.
- Leverage state-of-the-art machine learning and deep learning techniques, including large model technologies（LLM and MLLM, etc), to enhance recommendation performance and accuracy.
- Collaborate with cross-disciplinary teams, including infrastructure engineers, pmo, and researchers, to create advanced systems that improve recommendation relevance, diversity, and user engagement.

- Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, or a related field.

- Solid knowledge and experience with at least one major deep learning framework (e.g. PyTorch, Tensorflow, MXNet, Caffe/Caffe2).

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the NPI Team

The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission.

About The Role

This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity.

What You'll Do

- Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps.

- Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations.

- Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field.

- Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools.

- Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms.

- Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data.

- Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Raymond James is the place where good people grow and nowhere is that better demonstrated than in our internship program. During this immersive experience, you will engage with and implement the firm's core values through our five guiding behaviors. Featuring comprehensive orientation, onsite and remote training sessions in professional development, networking events, a speaker series, and volunteer opportunities, you will gain valuable knowledge of our business and culture while developing skills and relationships that support your future career.

To be eligible for the Summer 2027 Internship Program, you must be a junior-standing candidate pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.

Candidates who successfully complete the internship program may have the opportunity to transition into a full-time role at Raymond James following graduation.

Department Overview

Raymond James Bank's Private Client Banking (PCB) division supports the complex financial needs of clients by offering a comprehensive suite of lending and banking solutions, including Securities Based Lending (SBL), residential mortgages, tailored lending solutions and cash management products.

PCB combines field-based Banking Consultants with Home Office sales, analytics, pricing, product management, risk, finance, and operational support teams to deliver exceptional client outcomes.

This internship provides exposure to multiple areas of the lending business, including advisor engagement, sales enablement, pricing strategy, product management, business intelligence, portfolio analytics, and strategic decision making. Interns will gain hands-on experience supporting initiatives that drive growth, profitability, advisor adoption, and client engagement across the Securities Based Lending and Mortgage businesses.

Job Summary

Under general supervision, the Private Client Banking Strategy, Analytics & Sales Intern will support strategic initiatives across the Securities Based Lending (SBL), Mortgage, Margin, and Tailored Lending businesses. The intern will work closely with teams responsible for sales enablement, advisor support, education and engagement, pricing strategy, business analytics, portfolio management, product management, finance, and risk management.

This role combines analytical and business-focused responsibilities, including dashboard development, performance reporting, financial modeling, Return on Equity (ROE) analysis, pricing strategy, advisor support, educational content development, competitive research, and strategic project work. The intern will gain exposure to the full lending lifecycle and develop an understanding of how lending products are positioned, priced, managed, and supported across Raymond James Bank.

This internship is designed to provide meaningful exposure to lending product strategy, advisor engagement, pricing optimization, portfolio analytics, and business development, preparing participants for future careers within Raymond James Bank and the broader financial services industry.

Start Date: June 2, 2027 (based on internship program schedule)
End Date: August 13, 2027 (based on internship program schedule)
Work Schedule: Monday through Friday, up to 40 hours per week

Duties and Responsibilities

Analytics, Reporting & Business Intelligence

- Analyze lending, sales, operational, and portfolio data to support strategic initiatives and business decision-making.

- Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting solutions using Tableau, Excel, Qlik, SQL, Access, Power BI, and other business intelligence tools.

- Create reports measuring loan production, advisor adoption, utilization trends, commission activity, portfolio growth, profitability, and client engagement metrics.

- Support forecasting, financial modeling, performance measurement, and business case analyses.

- Collect, organize, validate, and analyze information from multiple data sources to ensure reporting accuracy and integrity.

- Prepare management reporting packages, executive summaries, and presentations highlighting business performance, key trends, and recommendations.

Securities Based Lending (SBL) Support

- Support the Securities Based Lending Consulting team by analyzing production metrics, advisor adoption trends, utilization rates, and portfolio performance.

- Assist with advisor and branch professional inquiries regarding SBL products, processes, educational resources, and sales support materials.

- Participate in portfolio reviews to identify growth opportunities and trends affecting client utilization and advisor adoption.

- Assist with annual reviews of discounted lending relationships and evaluate pricing performance and profitability implications.

- Support development and maintenance of advisor-facing SBL presentations, educational content, and communication materials.

- Conduct competitive analysis and market research related to securities-based lending products and pricing strategies.

Mortgage Business Support

- Analyze mortgage production, application volume, pipeline activity, referral trends, and funding performance.

- Assist in evaluating mortgage pricing competitiveness and business performance.

- Support mortgage reporting initiatives and performance tracking.

- Create advisor-facing educational materials and communications supporting mortgage solutions.

- Assist in measuring the success of mortgage campaigns, advisor engagement efforts, and growth initiatives.

- Collaborate with Mortgage Sales, Operations, and Product Management teams on strategic projects and process improvement initiatives.

Pricing Strategy & Product Management

- Support pricing activities for Securities Based Lending, Mortgage, Margin, and Tailored Lending products.

- Assist in pricing new loans utilizing Return on Equity (ROE) methodologies.

- Conduct profitability assessments, break-even analyses, and modeling of proposed pricing programs and promotional campaigns.

- Analyze portfolio performance and identify trends impacting product profitability and business growth.

- Assist Product and Pricing Strategy teams with product reviews, competitive assessments, and strategic initiatives.

- Support development of analytical tools and models designed to improve account-level pricing, portfolio management, and business insights.

- Recommend enhancements to reporting, modeling, and pricing tools that improve business decision-making.

Sales Enablement & Advisor Support

- Respond to routine inquiries from advisors, branch professionals, Banking Consultants, and internal business partners.

- Assist with development and distribution of educational materials, presentations, sales resources, and internal communications.

- Maintain communication hubs, reporting repositories, and shared team resources.

- Support coordination of meetings, webinars, training programs, educational events, and advisor engagement initiatives.

- Conduct market research and compile findings for strategic business projects.

- Collaborate with business partners to identify opportunities for process improvements and enhanced advisor experiences.

- Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of

- Fundamental concepts, practices, and procedures of a professional business environment.

- Financial services industry and advisor business models.

- Securities Based Lending, residential mortgage lending, margin lending, and structured lending concepts.

- Financial modeling, forecasting, portfolio management, and performance measurement techniques.

- Pricing strategy concepts including ROE, profitability analysis, spreads, and risk-adjusted returns.

- Large relational databases and business intelligence reporting tools.

- Data visualization and presentation best practices.

Skill in

- Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and other Microsoft Office applications.

- Tableau, SQL, Qlik, Power BI, and related reporting and analytics tools.

- Financial analysis, quantitative modeling, and analytical problem solving.

- Creating dashboards, performance reporting, and executive-level presentations.

- Researching, analyzing, and interpreting complex business information.

- Building effective relationships through a client-first, service-oriented mindset.

Preferred Technical Skills

- Advanced Excel capabilities including formulas, pivot tables, and data analysis.

- Tableau, Power BI, Qlik, or similar visualization platforms.

- SQL and database querying.

- Python, R, Power Query, or other analytical programming tools.

- PowerPoint and executive presentation development.

Ability to

- Analyze complex business problems and develop actionable recommendations.

- Interpret quantitative information and communicate insights effectively to technical and non-technical audiences.

- Prepare concise executive-level summaries and recommendations.

- Organize, prioritize, and manage multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment.

- Work independently and collaboratively across cross-functional teams.

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with advisors and internal business partners.

- Communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.

- Demonstrate initiative, adaptability, professionalism, curiosity, and attention to detail.

- Learn quickly and apply new financial, analytical, and business concepts.

Educational / Previous Experience Requirements

- Junior standing (December 2027 through May 2028 graduates) pursuing a bachelor's degree in Finance, Business Analytics, Economics, Accounting, Data Science, Business Administration, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field.

- Strong academic performance with demonstrated analytical aptitude preferred.

- Any equivalent combination of experience, education, and/or training approved by Human Resources.

- Eligible applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States and not require visa sponsorship now or in the future (including beyond OPT/EAD).

Develop and evaluate machine learning methods supporting small molecule design and synthesis. Working with public and internal chemistry datasets, the co-op will pursue a focused research project in either reaction prediction and benchmarking or molecular property prediction for medicinal chemistry optimization.

Potential projects include building benchmarks to assess reaction prediction models and reaction plausibility, or developing and fine-tuning molecular property predictors using project-specific data. Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our Electrical Validation teams measure, debug, and validate the electrical behavior of complex hardware platforms so products can move confidently through bring-up, validation, and release.

The opportunity

Join the Electrical Validation team and gain hands-on experience validating high-performance hardware. You’ll learn the team’s products, lab environment, measurement methods, firmware and update flows, and validation processes while contributing to a scoped project with a visible technical outcome.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys working close to the hardware: setting up an experiment, selecting the right instrument, collecting trustworthy data, analyzing the result, investigating unexpected behavior, and documenting what the team should do next. You’ll collaborate with Electrical Validation, firmware, system validation, ATE, PApps, program-management, and other engineering teams.

What you’ll do

- Learn the Electrical Validation environment, assigned product area, lab equipment, scripts, specifications, and project success criteria.

- Run repeatable electrical measurements and validation workflows for hardware platforms, boards, links, interfaces, or subsystems.

- Set up and use lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, BERTs, VNAs, power supplies, electronic loads, temperature chambers, probes, and related fixtures under engineering guidance.

- Collect, organize, and analyze voltage, current, timing, signal-quality, link, power, temperature, or other electrical data as appropriate for the project.

- Compare results with specifications, expected behavior, previous runs, and validation criteria; identify trends, anomalies, margins, and failure conditions.

- Support hardware bring-up and debug by checking connections, configurations, firmware or update flows, test scripts, instrument settings, and environmental conditions.

- Develop or improve Python, shell, or other automation scripts for measurements, data collection, report generation, or repeatability.

- Create clear data packages, validation reports, plots, checklists, Confluence pages, and handoff documentation that others can trust and reuse.

- Investigate defined technical issues, form evidence-based hypotheses, run focused experiments, and communicate recommended next steps.

- Collaborate with firmware, system validation, ATE, PApps, design, and other cross-functional teams to unblock shared execution and close assigned tasks.

- Keep project trackers, action items, and technical documentation current while communicating progress, blockers, and risks.

- Own a scoped validation workflow or product slice with increasing independence and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

- Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or a related field.

- Foundational understanding of circuits, electronics, digital systems, signal integrity, power, measurements, or hardware interfaces.

- Interest in learning how to use laboratory instruments and how to turn measurements into reliable engineering conclusions.

- Programming or scripting experience in Python, C/C++, MATLAB, shell, or another language used for automation and data analysis.

- Comfort learning in a Linux or technical lab environment and working with specifications, logs, plots, test procedures, and source control.

- A methodical approach to troubleshooting: verify the setup, isolate variables, collect evidence, compare against expectations, and document what changed.

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain results and uncertainty to cross-functional partners.

- Ownership, curiosity, humility, and persistence in an environment where experiments may need to be repeated and refined.

Helpful experience

- Oscilloscopes, BERTs, VNAs, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, or temperature chambers.

- High-speed serial links, PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, SERDES, clocking, jitter, eye diagrams, or signal-quality measurements.

- Board bring-up, firmware update flows, test fixtures, lab automation, or hardware debugging.

- Python data analysis, instrument control, report generation, or automated regression.

- Validation plans, test coverage, failure triage, data packages, or technical report writing.

- Jira, Confluence, Excel, Git, or other collaborative engineering workflows.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Equal opportunity

About the Team
The TikTok Model Infrastructure team is the core engine powering the world’s most engaged "For You" feed. We focus on the engineering efficiency and architectural evolution of recommendation models at an unprecedented scale. As we lead the industry’s shift toward LLM2Rec and Large Recommendation Models (LRM), our mission is to build ultra-high-performance infrastructure that bridges the gap between massive data scale and extreme algorithmic complexity.
We tackle the industry's most demanding "frontier" challenges: managing Petabyte-scale distributed embedding states, optimizing thousand-node GPU clusters, and perfecting real-time Sparse/Dense streaming. Our work ensures that models with hundreds of billions of dense parameters—on par with the world's largest LLMs—can operate with millisecond-level latency.

We are seeking Software Engineering Interns to join the Model Infra team to redefine the performance boundaries of recommendation systems. In this role, you will focus on the efficiency of the entire model lifecycle. - Hardware-Aware Co-Design: Work closely with researchers to design next-generation recommendation architectures optimized for modern GPU/NPU interconnects, ensuring high-bandwidth utilization across the cluster.

- Experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and a desire to "look under the hood" of model execution runtimes.
- A strong interest in solving system-level bottlenecks in large-scale distributed environments.

Preferred Qualification(s)
- Experience with Transformer-based architectures, 3D parallelism (TP/PP/DP).
- Deep understanding of the torch.compile stack, including TorchDynamo (graph acquisition) and TorchInductor (lowering).
- Hands-on experience writing high-performance kernels or optimizing collective communication (e.g., customizing NCCL/UCX).

Physical Design Engineer Intern (DM)

Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our silicon teams develop complex digital products where power, performance, area, timing, physical implementation, and manufacturability must come together reliably.

The opportunity

Join the Physical Design team and gain hands-on experience taking a digital design from RTL handoff through physical implementation and signoff. You’ll learn how physical design methodology and flow infrastructure turn design intent into an efficient, manufacturable layout while helping improve repeatability, productivity, and design quality.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys both engineering fundamentals and practical problem-solving: running a flow, reading timing and QoR reports, investigating a broken stage, adjusting constraints or configuration, and measuring the effect of an iteration. You’ll work with experienced physical design, CAD, front-end, STA, EMIR, and physical-verification engineers on a meaningful project.

What you’ll do

- Learn the physical design flow, development environment, project structure, tools, and methodology needed to contribute effectively.

- Run an assigned block through the RTL-to-signoff flow, including synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, optimization, timing closure, and signoff.

- Review physical design inputs such as RTL or netlists, SDC constraints, technology files, libraries, LEF/tech files, QRC data, and PDK-related inputs.

- Analyze timing, area, utilization, congestion, clock skew, insertion delay, transition, DRC, LVS, EMIR, and other quality-of-result reports.

- Help identify and resolve flow, implementation, timing, congestion, physical-verification, or infrastructure issues with guidance from experienced engineers.

- Support PPA exploration by running controlled experiments, comparing configurations, tracking results, and documenting the tradeoffs between power, performance, and area.

- Work with physical-design flow configuration, scripts, experiment definitions, reports, logs, and reproducible work areas.

- Contribute to CAD and flow infrastructure improvements such as report generation, run orchestration, validation checks, log mining, root-cause analysis, or handoff packaging.

- Use tools and flows such as Fusion, Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or related EDA environments under engineering guidance.

- Collaborate with front-end design, synthesis, STA, EMIR, physical verification, and other teams on inputs, handoffs, signoff criteria, and issue resolution.

- Participate in design reviews, code or flow reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.

- Deliver assigned physical-design work in a reproducible, well-documented state and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

- Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, VLSI, or a related field.

- Foundational understanding of digital logic, RTL, CMOS/ASIC design, computer architecture, timing, or semiconductor manufacturing.

- Interest in the physical implementation of digital designs and how layout decisions affect power, performance, area, timing, congestion, and manufacturability.

- Experience with Linux, command-line tools, source control, or scripting through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.

- A methodical approach to debugging: understand the inputs, reproduce the issue, inspect reports and logs, test a focused change, and evaluate the result.

- Ability to learn unfamiliar tools and technical concepts, ask focused questions, communicate progress and blockers, and follow through on commitments.

- Self-motivation, professionalism, ownership, and a collaborative mindset.

Helpful experience

- ASIC physical design, synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, timing closure, physical verification, or EMIR.

- Static timing analysis, multi-mode/multi-corner concepts, clock constraints, setup/hold analysis, slack, skew, or useful skew.

- Power planning, standard-cell placement, macro placement, congestion analysis, DRC/LVS, antenna checks, or power-integrity analysis.

- Tcl, Python, Bash, YAML, or other scripting and configuration languages used to automate engineering workflows.

- Synopsys Fusion Compiler, Cadence Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or comparable EDA tools.

- Git, Bitbucket, P4, Slurm, Snakemake, or other tools used for reproducible, compute-intensive engineering flows.

- Experience comparing QoR across experiments, generating reports, visualizing trends, or debugging flow infrastructure.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Equal opportunity

Astera Labs is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees. We value diverse perspectives and consider qualified candidates without regard to legally protected characteristics.

About Us

Integrate is building the first real-time, cross-boundary project management platform for the world’s most complex programs. We started with one of the most complex customers on earth, the U.S. government. Its programs span thousands of people, multiple organizations, billion-dollar budgets, and differentiated security environments. And somehow, too much of that work still runs on stale schedules, spreadsheets, hand-built slides, and project management software stuck in the Tetris era.

We’re changing that. Based in Seattle, Integrate has secured a $25 million U.S. Space Force contract and expanded across government and commercial programs, raised a $17 million Series A led by FPV Ventures, secured backing from J.P. Morgan, and built software that operates across government and commercial environments, from unclassified work to Top Secret networks.

We move fast, keep the egos low, and make room for quirks, strong opinions, fun, and the occasional chaos of building things from scratch with extreme velocity. We offer strong benefits, real ownership, and ambitious work with people you actually want to be around.

Our Solution

Integrate gives complex programs something they have never had before. One real-time schedule that can operate across organizations, security boundaries, and classification levels without fragmenting the schedule.

The program stays live as it changes. Teams can see how the program has moved, understand how a change ripples downstream, surface risk before it compounds, and control access down to the individual element. And our AI architecture works from that same continuously updated program state. It understands what is happening now, not a report assembled days or weeks ago. The schedule stops being a static plan and becomes a living reflection of the program itself.

We’re nowhere near done. We want to set a new standard for how the world’s most complex work gets done, and we won’t stop until we do.

About the Role

This is not a shadowing internship. From your first week, you'll contribute to real, customer-facing features that ship to production alongside the rest of our engineering team's work. We don't create separate intern projects. You'll work on the same product, tackle meaningful engineering challenges, and have the opportunity to see the impact of what you build.

As a growing startup, every engineer's contributions matter, including our interns. You'll work closely with experienced engineers, collaborate with product and design, and gain firsthand exposure to how technical and product decisions are made.

You'll also have support along the way, including weekly manager check-ins, a dedicated engineering buddy, and opportunities to learn through code reviews and team collaboration.

Our goal is for you to leave the summer having shipped meaningful work, grown as an engineer, and gained real-world experience building software used by teams developing rockets, robotics, and advanced manufacturing technologies.

What You’ll Work On

- Build and ship real features: Contribute to customer-facing functionality across our React and TypeScript frontend and our micro-service based architecture that includes languages such as Go, Python, and Rust.

- Own your work end-to-end: Participate in the full development lifecycle, from scoping and design through testing, deployment, and production.

- Collaborate across teams: Work alongside engineering, product, and design to solve problems, make thoughtful technical decisions, and participate in code reviews.

- Learn how we build and ship: Gain hands-on experience debugging production systems, monitoring performance, and deploy to multiple environments through a mature CI/CD pipeline.

- Make an impact: Share your work at our company-wide Feature Friday and contribute to engineering documentation and processes that help the team improve.

Tech Stack

Our core stack includes React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, Go, SQL, and REST. We also use GitHub Actions, Playwright, React Testing Library, Linear, and feature-flagged continuous deployment.

Internship projects typically involve a mix of 60% frontend and 40% backend, though this will vary based on team priorities and project needs.

What We're Looking For

We don't expect you to know everything. We're looking for students with a strong technical foundation, curiosity, and a willingness to learn.

- Currently a junior in an undergraduate program or pursuing a master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, with an expected graduation date within approximately 18 months.

- Working knowledge of React, TypeScript or JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3.

- Understanding of REST APIs and how frontend and backend systems work together.

- Exposure to Go, SQL, or another backend language through coursework, internships, or personal projects.

- Ability to navigate unfamiliar code, reason through problems, and learn new technologies quickly.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where priorities can shift and ambiguity is part of the process.

- Curious, proactive, and open to feedback. You're not afraid to ask questions, take initiative, and contribute ideas.

Nice to Have: Familiarity with Tailwind CSS, GitHub Actions, Playwright, or React Testing Library, as well as previous internship experience or substantial personal software projects.

Internship Details

- Duration: 12 weeks, June–September 2027, with flexible start and end dates to accommodate academic schedules.

- Compensation: $45/hour.

- Location: On-site in Seattle, WA. Interns must reside in the Seattle area for the duration of the internship.

- Holidays: Memorial Day (May 31), Juneteenth (observed June 18), Independence Day (observed July 5), and Labor Day (September 6).

- Interview Process: Technical Assessment, Recruiter Intro Call (Zoom with camera on), Team Member Interview (Zoom with camera on), and Final On-Site Technical Interview at our Seattle Office.

- Application Deadline: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until positions are filled. Early applications are encouraged.

ITAR Requirement

This position requires access to information protected under US export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and/or the Export Administration Regulations. As such, US person status (including US citizens, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted U.S. asylum status, or individuals admitted in U.S. refugee status) is a required qualification for this position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Integrate is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, genetics, or citizenship status (when otherwise legally authorized to work and access export-controlled data). We encourage applicants of all ages.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today.

In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team works on technologies that help people hear and communicate better in everyday life, from spatial audio to hearing assistance on AI glasses. Recent work includes Conversation Focus, which helps people hear the person they're talking to in noisy environments. As wearable devices become part of daily life, understanding how people actually listen, attend, and communicate in real-world settings is central to building audio experiences that adapt to each person.

We are looking for interns who want to model how people listen and communicate in the real world. Using multimodal, egocentric data from wearable devices (eye and head movement, speech and vocal behavior, gesture, and the acoustic scene), the intern will build models that infer listening and communication states such as auditory attention, listening effort, and conversational engagement. Ground truth for these states is often sparse or ambiguous. The goal is to inform hearing assistance and audio technologies that adapt to the listener.

The role suits candidates with a background in machine learning, computer science, hearing science, or auditory or cognitive neuroscience, who want to work at the intersection of those fields. Successful candidates will combine strong quantitative and machine learning skills with an understanding of human hearing and communication. Specific projects will be designed with successful applicants to match their skills and experience to current research needs.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities

Develop novel machine learning and statistical models that infer listening and communication behavior from multimodal wearable data (for example gaze, head movement, vocal cues, and turn-taking dynamics), with applications to hearing assistance. Relate model outputs to established hearing science measures, such as speech intelligibility, listening effort, and self-reported communication difficulty, to validate what the models capture. Design data collection strategies, benchmarks, and metrics for models trained on limited or ambiguous ground truth, including data from listeners with and without hearing loss. Design, run, and analyze human subjects experiments in laboratory and naturalistic listening environments. Collaborate with researchers and engineers across hearing science, audio signal processing, machine learning, and perception science. Communicate the research agenda, progress, and full analyses of results.

Qualifications

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a PhD in machine learning, computer science, hearing science, or auditory or cognitive neuroscience, or a related field 2+ years of experience with Python or a similar language for data analysis and modeling 2+ years of experience in statistical modeling and/or machine learning at the doctoral level, including time-series or sequential data Research experience with one or more of the following: multimodal behavioral data (e.g., eye tracking, motion, physiological, or speech signals), speech perception, auditory attention, or conversational communication Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment Proven track record of results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, or first-authored publications at venues such as ARO, ASA/JASA, Ear and Hearing, Trends in Hearing, JSLHR, ICASSP, Interspeech, ICMI, ETRA, CHI, NeurIPS, or similar Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, including multimodal or sequence models Experience with data from wearable or egocentric sensors (e.g., eye tracking, IMU, head-worn microphones), especially in naturalistic or conversational settings Experience with hearing-impaired populations, hearing aids, or cochlear implants Experience modeling under limited data, weak labels, or ambiguous ground truth Experience working with large, high-dimensional datasets from multiple sources Experience working and communicating cross-functionally in a team environment Intent to return to a degree program after the completion of the internship/co-op

About Mytra:

We’re creating an entirely new way to solve the most ubiquitous problem in industry - moving and storing material. We’re applying robotics and distributed software to create a new class of product for this $1T market. We’re focused on the supply chain industry first. The industry is in a massive bind with the continued growth of e-commerce, sharp rise in costs, and supply chain disruptions. What has been a “sleepy” industry for decades is now at the epicenter of sustaining the global economy.

About the role

This intern will participate as a team member of the robotics firmware team, contributing to the bring up of firmware components including hardware drivers, communication protocols, and controls functions that allow the robot to communicate, actuate, estimate, and meet the product specifications required for launch of the product.

What you’ll do:

- Support the development and tuning of motion control components for multi-axis robotic systems, including actuator control, trajectory generation, and path execution.
- Implement and test control loops for position, velocity, torque, and force control, and compare real-world behavior against model-based predictions.
- Contribute to state estimation work, including sensor fusion and Kalman filter–based estimators, in both simulation and on hardware.
- Work with distributed communication interfaces (e.g. CAN, NATS, ROS2) to move data between controllers, sensors, and actuators.
- Support motor and sensor bring-up, including calibration, diagnostics, and characterization of encoders, IMUs, and BLDC/stepper/servo drives.
- Iterate between simulation and hardware testing to reproduce corner cases, debug issues, and improve robustness.
- Write clear, maintainable C++ and Python for both real-time and high-level control software.

Ideal Candidates:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Physics, Computer Science, or a related field.
- Coursework or project experience in control theory, kinematics, dynamics, or system modeling for electromechanical systems.
- Proficiency in C/C++ and/or Python for embedded and/or high-level control software.
- Exposure to motor control (BLDC, stepper, servo) and sensor integration (e.g. encoders, IMUs, cameras) through coursework, labs, projects, or competition teams.
- Comfortable working in Linux-based development environments and with Git version control workflows.
- A bias toward simple, elegant, robust solutions over unnecessary control system complexity.
- Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to debug complex electromechanical systems at both the hardware and software level, often with limited telemetry.
- Demonstrated interest in approaching challenges with a physics-based, first-principles mindset.

Nice to have:

- Experience with real-time operating systems (e.g. FreeRTOS, RT Linux, Zephyr) or bare-metal embedded firmware.
- Familiarity with CAN, pub/sub communication frameworks (e.g. NATS, ROS2), or distributed control architectures.
- Hands-on experience implementing state estimation or control algorithms such as PID, trajectory generation, Kalman filtering, or localization.
- Familiarity with physics-based simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) or software-in-the-loop (SIL) testing, or CI/CD for robotics.
- Exposure to safety-critical system design standards (e.g. ISO 13849, IEC 61508).
- Experience with lab and embedded debugging tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG, or SWD.
- Prior internship, research lab, or competition experience (e.g. FIRST Robotics, FSAE, RoboMaster) building and debugging hardware systems.

A Final Note:

If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply — even if you don’t check every box. At Mytra, we build bots, but we hire humans. We value thoughtful challengers who communicate with clarity and respect, and we’re lifelong learners committed to getting better every day. We move fast, learn faster, and show up for each other under pressure. The best outcomes come from diverse perspectives working together to build something meaningful and built to last.

- Commuter benefits, including an up to $150 monthly commuter benefit
- Lively, modern combined office and lab space where we rapidly iterate through design, build, and test phases
- Fully equipped onsite gym and showers at headquarters

This role requires on-site presence at our Brisbane, CA headquarters, for close collaboration with the other teams.

$40-60 USD per hour (Mytra, Inc.)

About fab2

The fab2 team can build anything. We design all the hardware and software needed to make chips and we make the fabs, tools, and components ourselves.

We're looking for exceptional, hands-on people who can iterate to the limits of what's possible.

fab2 was founded by Sam Zeloof and Jim Keller. Sam is best known for making chips in his garage, and Jim has been a leader in the semiconductor industry for the past 40 years.

About the Role

We’re hiring Electrical Engineering Interns for the summer term. The internship begins in May or June, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. We’re rebuilding the chip fabrication process from the ground up, so you’ll be exposed to some really interesting and impactful work. You will work closely with other engineers to develop lithography systems, deposition tools, vacuum chambers, nanometer precision motion control, plasma etching systems, and related tools. You’ll be expected to identify problems, prototype solutions, productionize your prototypes, and deliver finished solutions that will revolutionize IC manufacturing.

Our philosophy is to get things built and tested in days or weeks, not months. Because of this, a portfolio is required to apply: show us the things you’ve actually built! If you’ve shipped a medium-to-high complexity system through a personal project or previous internship, you’d be a good fit here.

Responsibilities

- Design PCBAs and electrical systems for our machines, driving the end-to-end process including schematic capture, layout, bringup, testing, integration, and documentation.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with software, mechanical, and process teams to gather system requirements, performing independent investigations to define targets where requirements are ambiguous or missing.

- Investigate optimal design approaches and perform detailed analysis and simulations to evaluate electrical designs, weighing off-the-shelf components against custom solutions.

Required Experience

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree or higher in engineering

- Strong foundation in electrical engineering (KiCad/Altium, microcontrollers, embedded systems, digital circuits, etc.)

- Ability to learn quickly and troubleshoot technical problems

- Hands-on prototyping experience and the ability to move through design cycles quickly

Nice-to-have

- Familiarity with semiconductor processing— ALD, CVD, PVD, photolithography, etc.

- Hands-on experience with electromechanical assembly design and analysis from coursework, internships, or personal projects

We’re an early-stage hardware startup with solid funding, world-class advisors, and labs/offices in Austin, TX, Lockhart, TX, and San Francisco, CA. fab2 is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Human Computer Lab is a research lab building character robots that feel alive and responsive. Our first robot, LeLamp, explores a new category of consumer robotics where everyday objects become interactive and help us reshape our attachment to technology.

Our goal is to push the frontier of human-robot interaction by making technology more legible, emotionally intuitive, and human-centered. We are building the foundation for a new generation of robots designed for everyday environments.

What to expect

We’re looking for a controls/mechatronics engineer who wants to own the systems that make LeLamp move, respond, and feel alive. You’ll work at the intersection of hardware and software, designing and tuning control systems, integrating actuators and sensors, and debugging real hardware at the bench to translate intent into expressive motion. This is a high-ownership role working closely with the CEO and founding team across the full mechatronic stack, from low-level motor control and sensor fusion through to the higher-level behaviors that make the robot feel responsive and intentional in the real world.

In this role, you will:

- Design and tune control systems for actuated subsystems including motion control, feedback, and dynamic response.

- Integrate actuators, sensors, encoders, and embedded electronics into reliable mechatronic assemblies.

- Develop control algorithms in C++ and/or Python from simulation through deployment on hardware.

- Build and maintain URDF models and simulation environments aligned with the physical platform.

- Diagnose real-world control issues such as instability, backlash, latency, drift, and sensor noise.

- Collaborate with animators, mechanical and electrical engineers on actuator selection, structure, sensing strategy and motion fine-tuning

- Develop motion primitives and expressive behaviors that shape how the robot moves.

- Maintain documentation of control architecture and tuning decisions as the system evolves.

You may be a good fit if you:

- Are persuing a Bachelors/Masters in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Software Engineering.

- Have hands-on experience tuning control systems on real robotic hardware.

- Are fluent in C++ and/or Python for robotics or embedded control work.

- Have experience with ROS or ROS2 and real-time robotics software stacks.

- Are comfortable working with CAD tools such as SolidWorks or Onshape.

- Have experience with actuators, motor drivers, encoders, and IMUs across the full signal chain.

- Are strong at hardware debugging using tools like oscilloscopes and signal tracing.

- Have experience building URDF models and working with simulators such as Gazebo, MuJoCo, or Isaac Sim.

- Are comfortable working in environments where system architecture is still evolving.

- Have experience with impedance control, torque control, or whole-body control on physical robots

- Have experience with sensor fusion, state estimation, or Kalman filtering on hardware systems

- Have embedded programming experience on microcontrollers or DSPs in a controls context

- Have experience shaping expressive or character-driven robot motion

You will be a strong fit, if you:

- Are drawn to the physical reality of robotics. You want to see the system move, not just pass a simulation.

- Move quickly through iteration cycles and don't wait for perfect conditions to make progress.

- Take ownership over the feel of the robot's motion, not just its correctness.

- Work well in small, collaborative teams where controls, mechanical, and electrical are in constant conversation.

- Care about the person on the other end, and understand that how the robot moves is a big part of how it feels to live with.

The early team becomes the DNA of the company. We set ourselves and others to a high standard, and we respond with kindness when things get hard but keep everyone accountable. This requires us to be curious, creative, and diverse in our thinking and approach.

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, we encourage you to apply. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups often hold back unless they meet 100% of the criteria - we don’t want that to be the reason we miss out on great talent.

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

Join our group of passionate digital experts shaping the future of digital products from the USAA mobile app to our chat bot technologies. We are looking for a driven and enthusiastic Digital/Technical Product Manager Intern who is passionate about making an impact on the military community through the USAA mission.

This internship will be based at the USAA Corporate Headquarters in San Antonio, Texas.

What you’ll do:

- Empathize with and deeply understand the unique needs of end-users to determine the fastest path to deliver value.
- Translate business goals and end-user needs into a clear product vision, communicating direction and priorities to the development team, other matrixed teams, and third-party partners.
- Identify goals, metrics, and analytics to determine product value; continually make recommendations and refine the product backlog based on learnings.
- Manage and groom the product backlog, making decisions based on the value that will be delivered.
- Monitor research and the competitive landscape to recommend the best solutions and ensure that products remain or become best in class.
- Ensure that product directions balance user needs and business goals of driving new products, improving efficiency, and enhancing customer satisfaction.
- Work with design partners to formulate, test, and refine assumptions and hypotheses through user research.
- Collaborate with development teams to ensure smooth delivery and execution of product plans.

What You Will Learn:

- How to translate complex business goals into executable strategies.
- Learn how to take an idea through the refinement and development process.
- Best practices in user research and applying insights to product development.
- Techniques for managing a product backlog and prioritizing features.
- Financial planning and analysis in the context of product management.
- Conducting competitive analysis and strategic planning to keep products best in class.

What you need to have:

To qualify, you must be pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited college or university, and plan to graduate after the final day of the internship. Most of our interns participate the summer between their junior and senior years. Our 2027 internship will start on June 2, 2027 and last through August 13, 2027.

- Graduation date cannot be prior to August 13, 2027
- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
- Strong analytical skills and a passion for user-centric product design.
- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
- A proactive attitude with a desire to learn and take on new challenges.

What sets you apart:

- Academic concentration in Management Information Systems
- Graduation date between August 2027 and July 2028.
- Previous internships or project experience in coding languages
- Understanding of Agile methodologies
- First-hand knowledge of the military community

Compensation range: The salary range for this position is: $26.50 - $36.00. Interns will receive an intern stipend to assist with expenses.

USAA does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Please do not apply for this role if at any time (now or in the future) you will need immigration support (i.e., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT Training Plans, etc.).

Compensation: USAA has an effective process for assessing market data and establishing ranges to ensure we remain competitive. You are paid within the salary range based on your experience and market data of the position. The actual salary for this role may vary by location.

Employees may be eligible for pay incentives based on overall corporate and individual performance and at the discretion of the USAA Board of Directors.

The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.

Benefits: At USAA our employees enjoy best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellness. These benefits include comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans, 401(k), pension, life insurance, parental benefits, adoption assistance, paid time off program with paid holidays plus 16 paid volunteer hours, and various wellness programs. Additionally, our career path planning and continuing education assists employees with their professional goals.

For more details on our outstanding benefits, visit our benefits page on USAAjobs.com.

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis, this posting will remain open until the position is filled. Thus, interested candidates are encouraged to apply the same day they view this posting.

USAA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. - Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

- What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. About Firetiger

Firetiger is on a mission to help our customers build 1-person, $1 billion revenue companies.

We believe that eventually, all companies will be software companies, and the vast majority of coordination will be handled by autonomous agents, not people. To get there, we are helping software companies become "self-driving".

Legacy software engineering operations software is built for humans to manually explore data and patch together brittle alerts. The last generation of tools like Datadog is designed to enable humans to understand how software behaves. Firetiger flips the script. We approach operations from first principles: customers define top-down what success looks like for a business and product, then deploy agents to constantly monitor to ensure those goals are met and close the loop.

We are founded by Rustam and Achille, former leaders from Cloudflare and Segment, and backed by Sequoia Capital and founders and executives at Cloudflare, Segment, Amazon, Anthropic, Cursor, and Plaid.

We are looking for a Product Engineer to build the interfaces between humans and AI agents: the workflows, visualizations, and interaction patterns that make autonomous technical operations intuitive and actionable.

The Role

Firetiger's agents find production problems before your customers find them and your CEO hears about them. Here's how it works:

- We ingest telemetry with high-cardinality detail and automatically model what your system is and how it works

- Customers define objectives in natural language (e.g., "customers should have OAuth configured correctly") that stay relevant as infrastructure evolves

- Agents autonomously investigate issues, determine root cause, and take action to remediate

You'll build the product experiences that make this magic legible—turning complex autonomous investigations into something engineers actually want to use. You'll also build the agents themselves.

This is not a role where you implement specs handed down from product. You will own problems end-to-end: talking to customers, defining what to build, building it, and iterating until it's great.

What You Will Accomplish

- Agent interfaces: Design how engineers interact with AI agents operating their software systems. What should autonomous software operations look like? How do you give humans the right level of visibility and control?

- The agents themselves: Build the brains that turn messy natural-language objectives into the crisp outputs our customers rely on to run their businesses. You'll work on the core intelligence, not just the UI around it.

- Real-time collaboration tools: Create experiences where engineers can watch agents work, redirect wayward chains-of-thought, and collaborate on complex debugging sessions.

- Novel data exploration: Design new UX patterns for exploring high-cardinality data that agents surface. Think beyond traditional dashboards to new ways of understanding customer-specific issues at scale.

Who You Are

- High Agency: You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, whether a confusing user flow or missing feature, and you fix it. You ship.

- Product-Minded: You care about the why behind what you build. You talk to customers. You have opinions about what makes developer tools great vs. frustrating.

- Full-Stack Capable: You're comfortable working across the stack to deliver complete features. You've built complex, data-heavy web applications and know how to make them fast.

- AI-Curious: You've built with LLMs, or at a minimum collaborated with agentic development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc) to write software. You're excited about the design challenges of human-AI collaboration.

Qualifications

- Experience: You're excited about building and shipping user-facing software products. You have examples of projects you drove end-to-end that users loved.

- Communication: You can write a clear product spec, explain a technical tradeoff to a customer, and give direct feedback to teammates.

Compensation and Benefits

- $120k salary prorated for internship term

- In-person in San Francisco

How to Apply

We care more about your projects than your pedigree.

In your application, please include a link to something you've built: a side project, an open-source contribution, a product feature you're proud of. Show us how you think about building software products.

ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

As a Structural Analysis Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the Structural Analysis Team in performing detailed simulations and physics-based analysis and support the Vehicle Design and analysis activities. The Structural Analysis team is responsible for the analysis, design validation, and future improvements of our suite of Space Systems and Space Components.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results.

- Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an Aerospace, Aeronautical, Astronautical, or Mechanical engineering discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship

- GPA of 3.0 or above

- 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE

- 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)

- Experience using CAD/CAM

- Finite Element Analysis (FEA) software experience

- Statics and Dynamics experience.

- Siemens NX experience

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

- Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027

COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS

- Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly

- You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion.

Hourly Pay Range (CA Only)

$28—$28 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We have an opening for a Postdoctoral Researcher in the areas of atomistic and multiscale modeling to optimize metal joining in alloyed systems. The overarching goal of this project is to develop an integrated simulation-experiment workflow to maximize the utility of lab-scale tests by elucidating the fundamental scientific principles governing metal part joining. You will actively participate in the development of Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP) for large-scale atomistic modeling with quantum-mechanical accuracy for use in Grand Canonical grain boundary interface searches and the determination of subsequent interfacial properties. This work will occur in conjunction with mesoscale modeling and experimental teams to determine the effects of interfacial defects, impurities, phase transformations, and transient liquid phases on joining strength. The position is in the Materials Dynamics and Kinetics group of the Materials Science Division in the Physical & Life Sciences Directorate, supporting the Energetic Materials Center (EMC).

Depending on your assignment, this position may offer a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.

You will

- Perform and analyze first principles-based simulations (e.g., DFT, DFTB, etc.) to generate reference and validation data.
- Develop GPU-enabled MLIP models for complex intermetallic and alloyed systems for use in grain boundary and interface modeling.
- Provide inputs for mesoscale and thermodynamic modeling approaches, including mass transport properties and interfacial energies.
- Development and maintenance of our advanced atomistic simulation codes for interatomic model optimization and simulation.
- Aid in maintaining an organized and accessible materials data base for ML-driven experimental predictions.
- Document research; write and publish papers in peer-reviewed journals, and present results within the DOE community, at working group meetings, and at conferences.
- Pursue independent but complementary research interests and interact with a broad spectrum of scientists internally and externally to the Laboratory.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

- Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. Citizenship.
- PhD in Materials Science, Condensed Matter Physics, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field.
- Experience with scientific code development, including programming in python, C++, C, Fortran, and/or an equivalent level compiled language.
- Experience with electronic structure calculations using packages such as VASP, Quantum Espresso, or similar codes.
- Experience with molecular dynamics model development and applying atomistic machine learning methods for problems in chemistry or materials science.
- Experience with large-scale atomistic simulations in high-performance computing environments.
- Ability to develop independent research projects through publication of peer-reviewed literature.
- Proficient verbal and written communication skills as reflected in effective presentations at seminars, meetings and/or teaching lectures.
- Self-motivated and excellent interpersonal skills with desire and ability to work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary team environment.

Qualifications We Desire

- Experience with statistics-based simulations including (kinetic) Monte Carlo and enhanced sampling methods.
- Experience with computational workflow development and multiscale modeling integration.
- Experience with simulations of structurally/chemically disordered grain boundaries and heterogeneous interfaces.
- Experience with SI (Super Intelligence, formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence, or AI) and/or ML methods including surrogate modeling, feature engineering, generative models, Bayesian optimization, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, and Pareto front analysis.

Pay Range

$123,048 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

This is a Postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of extension to a maximum of three years. NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, MANUFACTURING - '26/'27

Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to serve populations with little or no connectivity. We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. - High volume production processes such as injection molding, high pressure die casting, and stamping

- Tool and die – the dies (molds and tools) that make those processes possible in-house

- Advanced machining processes, including 5-axis, EDM, gundrilling and more

- Investment casting – blades and vanes tooling and related process work

- Metrology and quality – GD&T, inspection, and capability on production hardware

- Completely new, ground up, green-field projects! Speccing new hardware and equipment, owning commissioning and initial process development

- Own manufacturing processes from process development through high-volume production

- Design and run trials to set process windows; measure yield, scrap, cycle time, and capability

- Develop fixtures, jigs, and work instructions operators use on the floor

- Apply CNC, metrology, and GD&T on real hardware

- Partner with Materials Engineering to develop and test advanced materials and manufacturing processes for next generation hardware

- Troubleshoot process and equipment problems on the floor and close root cause

- Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems

- Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline

- 1+ years of experience with engineering projects (internship or extracurricular experience is applicable)

- Graduating in the class of 2026 or 2027

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Hands-on work with manufacturing such as CNC and assembly

- Solid understanding of GD&T, metrology (go/no-go, micrometers, CMM), and how parts fail (scrap, dimensional, tool wear)

- Experience with CAD (NX or SolidWorks) and production drawings

- Experience with DOE, SPC/Cpk, or structured process trials on hardware

- Exposure to production machinery (injection molders, die casters, CNC, EDM, motion systems)

- Excellent communication skills both written and verbal

- Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Willingness to travel to other SpaceX sites and/or vendors for significant/extended periods of time (~15% travel normally, more during urgent manufacturing and test campaigns)

About Bridge Neurotech

Bridge Neurotech is building a non-invasive functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) platform with AI-based neural decoding for brain-computer interface applications. We are a seed-stage neurotechnology company developing technology that has the potential to transform how we interact with the human brain.

About the role

We are looking for a Hardware Engineering Intern to join Bridge for a six-month internship or co-op and help turn ideas into physical parts. Almost nothing we build can be bought, so we make our own as one-off or low-volume production, and you will work across all of it: design it, build it, test it, improve it.

This is a hands-on lab role with breadth: CAD in the morning, soldering in the afternoon, and Python scripting in between. We expect you to use AI coding tools to build automations and bespoke tools.

What you’ll do

- Design and iterate parts in CAD, for example probe housings, mounts, fixtures, enclosures, and lab hardware.

- Run our 3D printers: dial in materials and profiles, manage the queue, and keep turnaround measured in hours.

- Help build the automation around 3D printing and CNC, for example scripted slicing and job submission, print monitoring, and part tracking.

- Help develop processes for low-volume part production, for example molding, casting, potting, bonding, and the jigs and fixtures those processes need.

- Do the work that makes hardware real: soldering, cable and harness assembly, and careful assembly of delicate parts.

- Build test fixtures and benchtop setups, and help keep the lab organized and working.

- Write Python to glue the shop together: automation, instrument control, data logging, and inventory tracking.

- Work directly with our imaging scientists and research team to understand how each part will actually be used.

Who you are

Required

- Enrolled in a bachelor’s program in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related discipline, in your junior year or later, or in a master’s program.

- Available full time for six months.

- Working proficiency in CAD: parametric modeling, assemblies, and drawings.

- Hands-on 3D printing experience, for example tuning, troubleshooting, and repair.

- Comfortable soldering both boards and wire, and assembling precision hardware without breaking it.

- Some experience with Python: you can write a real script, for example file handling, an API call, or a serial interface.

- Comfortable using AI coding tools to get to working tooling.

- A bias toward building, testing, and improving over designing to completion first.

Nice to have

- PCB layout experience, particularly in Altium.

- CNC machining experience, for example CAM programming, fixturing, and workholding.

- Personal projects, a shop of your own, robotics or FSAE, or other evidence that you build things unprompted.

What we offer

- Six months of hands-on ownership of the hardware this company runs on.

- Mentorship from our engineers, and direct collaboration with our imaging scientists and research team.

- Work on a modality early enough that the tooling does not exist yet. Much of what you build will be the first of its kind.

Bridge Neurotech is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
